solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Champion runner an adulterer, they say

indicators.note: they say signals that the word for an adulterer is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: an adulterer is a cheater on their partner

explanation.surface: A star athlete is gossiped about as unfaithful to their spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheetah is the fastest land animal, so it is the supreme sprinter of nature.

clue.text: This property might cause gossip if it changed hands

indicators.note: changing hands means right is swapped for left, the letters R and L

parts.note: chatter is idle gossip

explanation.surface: Something owned might set tongues wagging when it is sold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed hands' looks like a sale; it swaps one hand for the other, R for L.
explanation.definitionFit: A chattel is an item of personal movable property.

clue.text: Problem created by monarch introducing tax? The opposite

indicators.note: introducing would put the tax into the monarch
the opposite reverses it, so the monarch goes inside the tax

parts.note: excise is a tax on goods
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A difficulty arises when the king brings in a new tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introducing' says the monarch takes in the tax; 'The opposite' flips it so EXCISE holds ER.
explanation.definitionFit: An exercise is a task or set problem for practice.

clue.text: English rush north for work

indicators.note: north in a down clue means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: to dart is to rush

explanation.surface: An Englishman hurries north for a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'north' reads EDART upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade is a skilled job or line of work.

clue.text: Later she's horribly cruel

indicators.note: horribly says the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Later on, a woman turns nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: A heartless person lacks compassion and is unkind or cruel.

clue.text: Charlie departs from Kentish Town in disguise

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: departs from means that letter leaves the town's name

parts.note: Dover is a port town in the county of Kent
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: Someone slips out of a town in Kent wearing a disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: Kentish Town is not the London district but a town in the county of Kent; the first impulse is to remove a C, but Charlie is added and the timetable D goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A cover is a false identity or front used to hide who someone really is.

clue.text: Apple from which grub might emerge?

definitions.meaning: a cooking apple, such as a Bramley
grub is slang for food, which comes out of a stove or oven

explanation.walkthrough: Grub in an apple suggests a maggot; here it is food from an oven.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a cooking apple and a kitchen stove.

clue.text: Frenzied sex over before period of abstinence

indicators.note: before puts the first pieces ahead of the fast in this down entry

parts.note: sex is Latin for six, VI in Roman numerals
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: Wild sex is done with before a time of self-denial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sex' is the Latin number six, VI, not intercourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Violent behaviour is wild and frenzied.

clue.text: Titian, easily irritated, blowing top

indicators.note: blowing top means losing the first letter, with a hint of losing one's temper

parts.note: crusty means short-tempered

explanation.surface: The painter Titian, short-tempered, loses his rag.
explanation.walkthrough: Titian is not the painter but the reddish-gold hair colour named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian is an auburn or red-brown colour, like rust.

clue.text: Honourable to support revolutionary in the long run

indicators.note: to support in a down clue puts the title beneath the revolutionary

parts.note: Jean-Paul Marat was a leader of the French Revolution

explanation.surface: A gentleman backs a rebel, hoping it pays off eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: A marathon is a running race of about 26 miles.

clue.text: Saw how old Bill is?

parts.note: a bill is an advertisement, AD for short
how old someone is gives their age

explanation.surface: Someone asks how old a man called Bill is.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill is not a man but a poster: an advert's age reads AD AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old proverb or saying, the same as an adage.

clue.text: Strangely, no US gaol area is comparable

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of these words are arranged in an odd new order

explanation.surface: An American prison oddly matches some other place.
explanation.definitionFit: Analogous things are similar or alike in some respect, so they can be compared.

clue.text: Piece — but not the leader?

indicators.note: but not the leader says the opening letter of the word for a piece is dropped

parts.note: a particle is a tiny piece of something

explanation.surface: A fragment, but not the one in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not the leader' drops P from PARTICLE. The whole clue also defines: a newspaper piece other than the leader, which is what British papers call the editorial.
explanation.definitionFit: An article is a written piece in a newspaper or magazine, and the leader is the editorial.

clue.text: For that reason I'm not sure about appearing in The Times

indicators.note: appearing in puts the hesitation inside the other words

parts.note: by means times, as in two by three

indicators.note: about means the hesitation sound is turned round

parts.note: er is the sound of someone unsure

explanation.surface: Someone hedges about featuring in The Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' is a multiplication sign here, as in two by three, not the newspaper; 'about' turns the hesitation round before it goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereby means by that means or as a result, so it gives the reason.

clue.text: Relation providing clue for spooks?

indicators.note: providing clue says the answer, read as an instruction, is itself the wordplay that leads to the next word

parts.note: spooks are spies, and SIS, the Secret Intelligence Service, employs them; half of the word sister spells those three letters

explanation.surface: A family member slips a hint to secret agents.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer read as wordplay, half of SISTER, gives SIS, Britain's foreign spy agency (MI6).
explanation.definitionFit: A sibling sharing only one parent is a close family member.

clue.text: Found here and there, as desert cat is

definitions.text: Found here and there, as desert cat is

indicators.note: found here and there says the letters of the next words are strewn about in a new order

explanation.surface: Wildcats of the desert are spread thinly across the land.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is the answer itself: the letters of 'desert cat' are found here and there, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Things spread about in no particular pattern, found in various places, are strewn or dispersed.

clue.text: A singer engaged in amorous activity

parts.note: the tit is a songbird

explanation.surface: A vocalist is caught up in a romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at it is a British euphemism for having sex.

clue.text: Study agreements head of state promoted

indicators.note: promoted in a down clue moves a letter higher, earlier in the word

parts.note: treaties are formal agreements between states

indicators.note: head of takes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A leader advances the cause of international accords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoted' moves the S of TREATIES up one place.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a written study of a subject.

clue.text: Sailor rejecting forgiveness, finding way out

indicators.note: rejecting has the sailor thrown out of the longer word

parts.note: absolution is forgiveness of sins
AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A seaman refuses pardon and finds an escape.
explanation.definitionFit: A solution is the answer to a problem, a way out of it.

clue.text: What's put on table occasionally annoys husband

indicators.note: occasionally takes only every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: Whatever is served at dinner sometimes irritates the husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is British slang for food, which is what gets served at the table.

clue.text: Two Gentlemen of Verona?

parts.note: the Shakespeare title read literally: men in an Italian city, called by the Italian plural for gentlemen

explanation.walkthrough: The play title is a red herring: any two men in Verona would be addressed in Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Signori is the Italian for gentlemen or sirs, plural of signore.

clue.text: Hot-headed peasants roughly grabbing one with nothing

indicators.note: grabbing has the shuffled letters take hold of the other pieces
roughly says the letters are put in a loose, rearranged order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Angry peasants seize a man who owns nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' makes PASSNATE from PEASANTS, and 'grabbing' puts I and O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone passionate has strong, fiery feelings, as a hot-headed person does.

clue.text: A reporter's pushiness causing offence

indicators.note: a reporter's words are spoken, so the phrase is heard not read

parts.note: a front is cheek or boldness, brass neck

explanation.surface: A journalist's brashness upsets people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reporter's' says the phrase is heard: A FRONT said aloud is the answer, spelt with a double F.
explanation.definitionFit: An affront is an insult that causes offence.

clue.text: Fortune down to Dutch ancestry in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Luck is blamed on someone's Dutch roots.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Fortune down' as the definition; the answer means only fortune, and 'down to' is a link phrase meaning owing to.
explanation.definitionFit: Chance is luck or fortune, what happens without design.

clue.text: One who's directing sexist perhaps to keep quiet

indicators.note: to keep puts the quiet word inside the other

parts.note: a sexist is an example of a bigot
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A chauvinist is told to hold his tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: A big shot is an important person who is in charge of things.

clue.text: Centre succeeded in time of growth

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the other word

parts.note: a boom is a period of economic growth
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, in family trees

explanation.surface: A central figure prospered during a good spell.
explanation.definitionFit: The bosom of something is its heart or centre, as in the bosom of the family.

clue.text: I couldn't care less what you might do with Olive

definitions.text: what you might do with Olive
definitions.meaning: an olive is often stuffed, with pimento for example

explanation.walkthrough: The capital O makes Olive look like a woman's name; it is the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a rude brush-off and an instruction to fill a pitted olive.

clue.text: About 50 soldiers going to a dance

indicators.note: about has the soldiers go around the number

parts.note: the SAS is the British Special Air Service
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Roughly fifty troops head off to a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About 50' looks like a rough count; 'About' puts SAS around L.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a lively Latin American dance.

clue.text: Suspect cold nurse is a rogue

indicators.note: suspect, as an adjective meaning dodgy, says the letters are not in their proper order

explanation.surface: A chilly nurse comes under suspicion as a villain.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoundrel is a dishonest, unprincipled person, the same as a rogue.

clue.text: Shackles press savagely at first

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them

indicators.note: at first takes just the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Restraints are clamped on savagely at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Irons are metal fetters or chains for prisoners.

clue.text: State of shock yours truly's in

indicators.note: in says the self-reference goes inside the hair

parts.note: a shock of hair is a mane
yours truly is the speaker, I

explanation.surface: The writer admits to being in a state of shock.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is a state of the USA in New England.

clue.text: On return, keep catching fish — in this?

definitions.text: On return, keep catching fish — in this?

indicators.note: on return says the whole result is read backwards
catching puts the fish inside the other word

parts.note: to tend is to keep or look after
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: Keep hauling fish in on the way back — with this net?
explanation.walkthrough: Keep means tend, as shepherds keep their flocks. The whole clue also describes the net the fish are caught in.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragnet is a net pulled along the bottom to catch fish.
